# The construction {#sec-sm-construction}

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon=false title="Learning goals"}
- Assemble a soliton S-matrix from an R-matrix, a gradation and a scalar factor.
- Impose unitarity and crossing, and see what they leave undetermined.
- Fix the remaining freedom by the soliton masses, and test the result against the particle S-matrices through the breathers.
- Work through the construction for $a_n^{(1)}$, where every step can be done by hand.
:::

@sec-qg-symmetry showed that soliton S-matrices have the form $\Phi\,\check R$. This chapter turns that observation into a procedure. It is the procedure used for every new S-matrix in this part, and it reproduces the known ones. The worked example in @sec-an-example applies it to $a_n^{(1)}$, Hollowood's case, where the R-matrix is the simplest one beyond sine-Gordon.

Every amplitude in this part is built in the same five steps. The case-specific inputs are the representation, the R-matrix and the integer lifts of the scalar factor's zeros.

## Amplitude, gradation and rapidity variable {#sec-amplitude-and-gradation}

A soliton multiplet is a finite-dimensional representation $V(x)$ of $U_q(\hat{\mathfrak g}^\vee)$, with $x$ the spectral parameter. The two-soliton amplitude is

$$
S_{ab}(\theta)=\Phi_{ab}(\theta)\,\check R_{ab}\big(x(\theta)\big),\qquad x(\theta)=e^{2T\theta}.
$$

Here $\check R_{ab}$ maps $V_a(x)\otimes V_b(1)$ to $V_b(1)\otimes V_a(x)$ and is normalised to 1 on the highest-weight channel. Gandenberger, MacKay and Watts [@gmw1996] fix the gradation from the Lorentz spins of the non-local charges:

$$
2T=\frac{4\pi h}{\beta^2}-h^\vee .
$$

In this formula $h$ and $h^\vee$ are the Coxeter and dual Coxeter numbers of $\hat{\mathfrak g}$. For twisted $\hat{\mathfrak g}=X^{(k)}$ the formula holds with $\beta^2$ replaced by $\beta_{\rm lit}^2=\beta^2/k$ (@sec-conventions) and with Kac's dual Coxeter number $h^\vee$ (@sec-qg-gradation). With $\omega=4\pi/\beta^2-1$ in the normalization of @sec-lie-algebraic-data, we write $q=-e^{-i\pi\omega}=e^{-4\pi^2i/\beta^2}$, the value (-@eq-q-physical) of Bernard and LeClair for the coproduct of the non-local charges, and use the rapidity variable $t=T\theta/(i\pi)$, so that $x=e^{2\pi i t}$ and the physical strip is $0<t<T$. A pole of $\check R$ at $x=\varepsilon q^{-l}$ then corresponds to positions $t\equiv l(\omega+1)/2+\arg(\varepsilon)/2\pi \pmod 1$. All the poles tabulated in this part have even $l$, where this is $t\equiv l\omega/2+\arg(\varepsilon)/2\pi$.

## Unitarity and crossing {#sec-unitarity-crossing}

With the normalisation above, $\check R(x)\check R(1/x)=1$, so unitarity requires $\Phi(\theta)\Phi(-\theta)=1$. The dual representation satisfies $V^*(x)\cong V(x\,x_c)$ for a unique crossing point $x_c$, which we compute numerically in each case. The universal R-matrix then gives

$$
\big(R(x)^{-1}\big)^{t_1}=c_u(x)\,(C^{-1}\otimes 1)\,R(x\,x_c)\,(C\otimes 1),
$$

with $c_u$ rational in $x$. Crossing requires $x(i\pi)=x_c$, which links $T$ to $\omega$, and $\Phi(i\pi-\theta)=\Phi(\theta)\,c_u\big(1/x(\theta)\big)$.

## The scalar factor {#sec-scalar-factor}

Following [@gmw1996], we take $\Phi=F=c\,f$, where $c$ vanishes at every pole of $\check R$:

$$
c(t)=\prod_j\sin\pi(t-a_j),\qquad f^{(1)}(t)=\pi^{-N}\prod_j\Gamma(t-a_j)\,\Gamma(1+t+a_j),
$$

$$
f(t)=\prod_{k\ge1}\frac{f^{(1)}\big(t+2T(k-1)\big)\,f^{(1)}\big(-t+2T(k-\tfrac12)\big)}{f^{(1)}\big(t+2T(k-\tfrac12)\big)\,f^{(1)}\big(-t+2Tk\big)} .
$$

The product makes $f(T-t)=f(t)$ and $f(t)f(-t)=1/\big(c(t)c(-t)\big)$, so $F$ is unitary and carries the crossing factor. Then $c\,\check R$ has no poles at all. The only physical-strip poles of $S$ come from the Gamma functions, at $t=a_j-k$ with $k=0,1,2,\dots$, and their crossed images. At $t=a_j$ the residue is $\check R$'s residue at the corresponding R-matrix pole, so it projects onto the bound-state multiplet.

## The integer lifts {#sec-integer-lifts}

Crossing fixes each $a_j$ only modulo 1. Shifting $a_j$ to $a_j+1$ multiplies $F$ by the crossing-symmetric unitary CDD factor $(a_j+1)(T-a_j-1)$, in the block notation of @sec-breather-test. This moves the top of the $j$-th pole tower by one step, which changes the corresponding bound-state mass at order $\beta^2$.

We fix the lifts by one principle: the fusion angles must make the soliton mass ratios equal, exactly, to the particle mass ratios of the same theory. For $c_n^{(1)}$ and $a_{2n-1}^{(2)}$ this is equivalent to $T-a_j$ being an integer multiple of $\omega+\tfrac12$.

## The breather test {#sec-breather-test}

The singlet channel of the soliton $n$ with itself has a tower of breather poles, the lowest at $t=T-1$. Its residue is rank one. Because a breather is a singlet, its scattering with a soliton is a scalar times the identity. Breather–breather amplitudes then follow by multiplying two shifted breather–soliton scalars, with no further numerics. All of these are finite products of the blocks

$$
(y)=\frac{\sinh\!\left(\frac{\theta}{2}+\frac{i\pi y}{2T}\right)}{\sinh\!\left(\frac{\theta}{2}-\frac{i\pi y}{2T}\right)},\qquad (y)(-y)=1,\quad (y+2T)=(y),\quad (T)=-1 .
$$

We compare these products, in exact arithmetic in $\omega$, with the Delius–Grisaru–Zanon (DGZ) [@dgz1992] and Corrigan–Dorey–Sasaki (CDS) [@corrigan1993] particle S-matrices. A DGZ/CDS block $(x)_H$ corresponds to our block $(y)$ with $y/T=x/H$.

## The crossing sign {#sec-crossing-sign}

Our numerical crossing test compares $S(i\pi-\theta)$ with $(C\otimes 1)\,S_{21}(\theta)^{t_1}\,(C^{-1}\otimes 1)$, and returns the ratio of the two as a number $\kappa$. With $q=-e^{-i\pi\omega}$ it returns $\kappa=+1$ for the $c_n^{(1)}$ spinor, $n=1,2,3,4$, and for the $a_5^{(2)}$ spinor, so these amplitudes are crossing symmetric with the scalar factor $c\,f$ and no extra CDD factor. For $n=1$ the amplitude is Zamolodchikov's (-@eq-sg-smatrix).

The test detects the sign of $q$. The crossing point, $T$, the eigenvalues of $\check R$, the zeros $a_j$ and $c\,f$ depend on $q$ only through $q^2$. But $q\to-q$ conjugates $\check R$ by a diagonal sign matrix on $V\otimes V$ that is not a product of one-soliton basis changes. For sine-Gordon it reverses $S_T$ relative to $S_R$ (@sec-six-vertex). It also multiplies $c_u$, and with it $\kappa$, by $(-1)^n$ for the $c_n^{(1)}$ spinor, and by $-1$ for the $a_5^{(2)}$ spinor. A computation with $q=e^{-i\pi\omega}$, minus the physical value, therefore gives $\kappa=(-1)^n$ for the $c_n^{(1)}$ spinor. That amplitude describes the same particles with the opposite relative exchange sign of solitons and antisolitons; for $n=1$ it is Zamolodchikov's with $S_T\to-S_T$. For all the representations computed, the change of $\kappa$ under $q\to-q$ is $(-1)^{2(\lambda,\rho)}$, with $\lambda$ the highest weight of the horizontal representation in the normalization in which the short roots have squared length 2 [Conjecture]. For the $b_n$ spinors $2(\lambda,\rho)=n^2$.

## Worked example: the $a_n^{(1)}$ solitons {#sec-an-example}

For $a_n^{(1)}$ the algebra is self-dual, so the soliton symmetry is $U_q(a_n^{(1)})$ itself, and the solitons of species $a$ form the fundamental representation $V_a=\Lambda^a\mathbb C^{n+1}$ (@sec-qg-consequences). Hollowood [-@hollowood1993b] constructed their S-matrices. We follow the steps of this chapter for the species-1 solitons.

**Gradation.** With $h=h^\vee=n+1$, the formula of @sec-amplitude-and-gradation gives $2T=h\big(\frac{4\pi}{\beta^2}-1\big)=h\omega$, with $\omega=\frac{4\pi}{\beta^2}-1$. For $n=1$, $T=\omega=\lambda$, the sine-Gordon value (@sec-qg-gradation).

**R-matrix.** $V_1\otimes V_1$ is the sum of the $q$-symmetric and $q$-antisymmetric tensors, and the tensor-product graph gives Jimbo's R-matrix (@sec-tpg),

$$
\check R_{11}(x)=P_{\rm sym}+\rho(x)\,P_{\rm antisym},
$$

with $\rho$ the six-vertex eigenvalue (-@eq-six-vertex-eigenvalue) for every $n$. With the coproduct of this part, which replaces $q$ by $q^{-1}$ relative to @sec-six-vertex, $\rho$ has its pole at $x=q^{-2}$ and its zero at $x=q^{2}$. Both depend only on $q^2$. The residue at the pole projects onto the antisymmetric tensors, which are $V_2=\Lambda^2\mathbb C^{n+1}$.

**Bound states.** The pole $x=q^{-2}$ lies at $t\equiv\omega\pmod1$. With $2T=h\omega$, the value $t=\omega$ corresponds to

$$
\theta=\frac{i\pi t}T=\frac{2\pi i}h ,
$$

which is exactly the fusing angle $u_{11}^2$ of the particles of $a_n^{(1)}$ (@sec-an-smatrix). So the bound state $1+1\to2$ appears at a coupling-independent angle with the right multiplet, and its mass is $M_2=2M_1\cos\frac\pi h$. Continuing by fusion (@sec-fusion), the species-$a$ soliton has

$$
M_a=M_1\frac{\sin(\pi a/h)}{\sin(\pi/h)} ,
$$

the classical ratio, now exact. No integer lift is needed: the scalar factor can place its zero at $t=\omega$ itself. This is special to the self-dual, simply-laced case. In Chapters [-@sec-sm-cn]–[-@sec-sm-f4] the lifts are what decides the masses.

**Crossing.** The dual of $V_1$ is $V_n$, the antisoliton. Crossing therefore relates $S_{11}$ to $S_{1n}$, and the crossing point $x(i\pi)=e^{2\pi iT}=e^{i\pi h\omega}$ is a power of $q$, as @sec-qg-crossing requires. The scalar factor is fixed by unitarity, crossing and minimality as an infinite product of Gamma functions, given explicitly by Hollowood [-@hollowood1993b].

**Breathers.** In the soliton–antisoliton channel $V_a\otimes V_{\bar a}$ the singlet carries towers of breather poles. Gandenberger [@gandenberger1995] showed that the lowest breathers scatter as the particles of $a_n^{(1)}$ with the S-matrix (-@eq-an-smatrix) continued to imaginary coupling, the first instance of the breather–particle identification beyond sine-Gordon.

**Check: $n=1$.** For sine-Gordon $V_1\otimes V_1$ is spin $\frac12\otimes\frac12$, $T=\lambda$, and the antisymmetric pole at $t=\omega$ corresponds to $\theta=i\pi$, the edge of the physical strip: two solitons do not bind, as they should not. The breather towers of the scalar factor lie at $t=T-k$, $k=1,2,\dots$, which are the poles $\theta=i(\pi-k\xi)$ of the Zamolodchikov S-matrix (@sec-qg-gradation).

## Exercises {#sec-sm-construction-exercises}

::: {#exr-scalar-unitarity}
Show that $f$ as defined in @sec-scalar-factor satisfies $f(T-t)=f(t)$ and $f(t)f(-t)=1/\big(c(t)c(-t)\big)$, using only the functional equation of the Gamma function.
:::

::: {#exr-lift-cdd}
Show that shifting a zero $a_j\to a_j+1$ multiplies $F$ by a crossing-symmetric, unitary CDD factor. Express it in terms of the blocks $(y)$ of @sec-breather-test.
:::

::: {#exr-an-fusing}
For $a_n^{(1)}$, verify that the pole of $\check R_{11}$ at $t=\omega$ gives $\theta=2\pi i/h$ for every coupling, and derive $M_a/M_1=\sin(\pi a/h)/\sin(\pi/h)$ by repeated fusion.
:::

::: {#exr-block-translation}
Show that a DGZ/CDS block $(x)_H$ equals the block $(y)$ of @sec-breather-test when $y/T=x/H$. What does this say about the relation between $T$, $H$ and the breather masses?
:::

## Notes and references {#sec-sm-construction-notes}

The general structure $S=\Phi\check R$ goes back to Zamolodchikov and Zamolodchikov's sine-Gordon S-matrix [@zz1979], was developed for affine Toda solitons by Hollowood [@hollowood1993a; @hollowood1993b], and was put on a Hopf-algebraic footing by Delius [-@delius1995]. The form of the scalar factor as $c\,f$ with Gamma functions is that of Gandenberger, MacKay and Watts [@gmw1996]. The use of the soliton masses to fix the integer lifts, and the breather test against the DGZ and CDS amplitudes in exact arithmetic, are new here.
